name: Convex Analysis and Optimization (6.253)
description: Convexity, duality, and the theory behind the optimization I use in practice. Studying convex sets, subgradients, and Lagrangian duality gave me the vocabulary to reason about why an algorithm converges, not merely that it does.

name: Linear Algebra (18.06)
description: The grammar of nearly everything computational, from least squares to the singular value decomposition. Working through matrix factorizations changed how I see data, as geometry waiting to be read rather than numbers waiting to be stored.

name: Introduction to Probability (STAT 110)
description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts and techniques of probability theory. This course covers random variables, distributions, and limit theorems.
